lines.text: | **D2** | divine Spirit — **from context** | an action or attribute in the verse that the text elsewhere gives to God's Spirit, or the adjacent verse names it (e.g. Luk 2:27 after 2:25–26) |
| **T** | **temper** (rûaḥ = anger / self-control) | H7307J; one case (Mic 2:7) is the **Lord's** temper |
| **B** | **boundary** | God-given breath/spirit in the human: "the spirit of God is in my nostrils" (Job 27:3) |
| **D-attr** | divine **as attributed by a pagan speaker** | "the spirit of the holy gods is in you" (Daniel 4–5) |
A verse can carry **two classes** where two referents are present, e.g. Rom 8:16 "The Spirit himself [D1] bears witness with our spirit [H1]".
- Could be the person's own spirit (cf. 1Co 14:14 "my spirit prays") or God's Spirit.
- The ESV reads these as divine. The verses alone don't decide it, although the paragraphs contain explicit D1 verses (Gal 4:6; Rom 8:9).
- 1Pe 3:18; 4:6; 1Co 15:45 ("a life-giving spirit"); 1Ti 3:16 ("vindicated by the Spirit / in spirit").
- Also Rom 1:4 ("Spirit of holiness") and Heb 9:14 ("eternal Spirit"), which are debated.
- Jam 4:5 ("the spirit that he has made to dwell in us"); Rom 8:10 ("the Spirit/spirit is life"); Rom 2:29 (circumcision "by the Spirit / in spirit").
- 1Co 6:17 ("one spirit with the Lord") is a genuine boundary: the human spirit is joined to the Lord.
- 1Co 12:10; 1Jo 4:1; 2Th 2:2; 2Co 11:4 ("a different spirit"); Rev 19:10 ("the spirit of prophecy").
**f. "Seven spirits (of God)"** — Rev 1:4; 3:1; 4:5; 5:6
- Ecc 8:8 ("No man has power to retain the spirit"); Ecc 11:5 ("the spirit comes to the bones in the womb"); Job 34:14 ("gather to himself his spirit and his breath" — God's own, or the one he gave).
- Eze 2:2; 3:24 ("the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet") — D3.
- Num 27:18 ("a man in whom is the Spirit").
- 1Ch 28:12 ("all that he had in mind" = "by the spirit" [lexical]).
- Hos 9:7 ("the man of the spirit").
- Eph 1:17 ("the Spirit/a spirit of wisdom and revelation"); 2Co 4:13 ("spirit of faith"); Isa 4:4 ("spirit of judgment / burning"); Jer 51:1 ("spirit / wind of a destroyer").
- **Witness together:** "The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit" (Rom 8:16).
- **Knowing by analogy:** "the spirit of that person, which is in him … the Spirit of God" (1Co 2:11).
- **Exchange:** the Spirit of the Lord departs; a harmful spirit from the Lord comes (1Sa 16:14).
- **Contrast:** "spirit of slavery" vs "Spirit of adoption" (Rom 8:15); "spirit of the world" vs "Spirit who is from God" (1Co 2:12); "Spirit of truth" vs "spirit of error" (1Jo 4:6).
- **Co-presence:** the Spirit lifts the prophet, who goes "in the heat of my spirit" (Eze 3:14); the Spirit of the Lord falls on Ezekiel, and God knows "what comes into your mind [rûaḥ]" (Eze 11:5).
- **Creation:** "The Spirit of God has made me" // "the breath of the Almighty gives me life" (Job 33:4).

4. **Boundary cases (B, and some U) sit exactly where God's giving meets human life:** breath in the nostrils (Job 27:3), the spirit returning to God (Ecc 12:7, H2), the spirit God "made to dwell in us" (Jam 4:5).
5. **Divine temper.** H7307J is used once of the Lord: "Has the Lord grown impatient?" (Mic 2:7). ◆ fringe.

findings.text: c. Christ and the dead "made alive / living in the spirit" — spirit as a mode of existence: 1Pe 3:18; 4:6; 1Co 15:45 ("a life-giving spirit"); 1Ti 3:16 ("vindicated by the Spirit / in spirit").; Also Rom 1:4 ("Spirit of holiness") and Heb 9:14 ("eternal Spirit"), which are debated.

d. Human spirit or Holy Spirit indwelling: Jam 4:5 ("the spirit that he has made to dwell in us"); Rom 8:10 ("the Spirit/spirit is life"); Rom 2:29 (circumcision "by the Spirit / in spirit").; 1Co 6:17 ("one spirit with the Lord") is a genuine boundary: the human spirit is joined to the Lord.
e. Prophetic "spirits" to be tested: 1Co 12:10; 1Jo 4:1; 2Th 2:2; 2Co 11:4 ("a different spirit"); Rev 19:10 ("the spirit of prophecy").
f. "Seven spirits (of God)" — Rev 1:4; 3:1; 4:5; 5:6: The "of God" marker is present, but the plural leaves divine Spirit vs angelic spirits open.

g. Life-breath vs spirit: Ecc 8:8 ("No man has power to retain the spirit"); Ecc 11:5 ("the spirit comes to the bones in the womb"); Job 34:14 ("gather to himself his spirit and his breath" — God's own, or the one he gave).

h. Old Testament "the Spirit" without a marker, where the prophet's own spirit is also possible: Eze 2:2; 3:24 ("the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet") — D3.; Num 27:18 ("a man in whom is the Spirit").; 1Ch 28:12 ("all that he had in mind" = "by the spirit" [lexical]).; Hos 9:7 ("the man of the spirit").

i. "Spirit of X" where the X could be divine or a disposition: Eph 1:17 ("the Spirit/a spirit of wisdom and revelation"); 2Co 4:13 ("spirit of faith"); Isa 4:4 ("spirit of judgment / burning"); Jer 51:1 ("spirit / wind of a destroyer").

4. What the distinction shows [Claude reading]: The Hebrew human spirit is prominent. In H7307G the human spirit (H1 + H2, about 90 rows) is at least as present as the divine Spirit (D1 + D2, about 70 rows). In the Greek G4151G the divine Spirit dominates, and the human spirit is a minority (about 50 rows).; Dispositions (X) are almost all Hebrew: jealousy, whoredom, confusion, deep sleep, justice, skill, wisdom, grace. The same construction ("a spirit of …") sits on the boundary between a mood that arrives and a being that is sent (§3i).; Many verses carry two spirits at once. These are the clearest evidence of how the text relates them: Witness together: "The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit" (Rom 8:16).; Knowing by analogy: "the spirit of that person, which is in him … the Spirit of God" (1Co 2:11).; Exchange: the Spirit of the Lord departs; a harmful spirit from the Lord comes (1Sa 16:14).; Contrast: "spirit of slavery" vs "Spirit of adoption" (Rom 8:15); "spirit of the world" vs "Spirit who is from God" (1Co 2:12); "Spirit of truth" vs "spirit of error" (1Jo 4:6).; Co-presence: the Spirit lifts the prophet, who goes "in the heat of my spirit" (Eze 3:14); the Spirit of the Lord falls on Ezekiel, and God knows "what comes into your mind [rûaḥ]" (Eze 11:5).; Creation: "The Spirit of God has made me" // "the breath of the Almighty gives me life" (Job 33:4).; Boundary cases (B, and some U) sit exactly where God's giving meets human life: breath in the nostrils (Job 27:3), the spirit returning to God (Ecc 12:7, H2), the spirit God "made to dwell in us" (Jam 4:5).; Divine temper. H7307J is used once of the Lord: "Has the Lord grown impatient?" (Mic 2:7). fringe.
